why_it_discriminates: The file looks normal in an editor, so the agent has to look at its bytes: it starts with a UTF-8 byte-order mark and ends its lines with CRLF. The reader opens files as bytes (for .gz and corrupt bytes) and strips only \n, so every line keeps a trailing \r that the parser's `ms$` anchor rejects. Fixing only that (rstrip, strip(), a looser regex) still leaves the first line malformed, because str.strip() does not remove U+FEFF, and the prompt says every line is a real request. Converting the sample file instead of the code, or switching only plain files to text mode, also fails. The hidden check feeds one log as LF, CRLF, BOM+CRLF, BOM+LF, mixed endings, no final newline, and gzipped, and requires output byte-identical to what the fixture prints for the LF file today, with its genuinely malformed lines still counted.
